conflict_topics: Strong-smelling cooking (sambal belacan) vs shared flat comfort
Mitigation measures (window open, closing doors, notifying laundry)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants gave concrete, context-specific reasons (work calls, laundry location) which grounded proposals.
Conversation progressed from complaint to concrete compromise within a few turns without side arguments.
Minimal needless repetition; most turns added new information or proposals.
Resolution was explicit and mutually accepted in participants' own words.
evaluation.final_reason: All four verbally agreed to a concrete arrangement: Agent A summarized 'So if you cook after 7 pm with the window open and let Agent C know beforehand, that works for everyone?' Agent B: 'Yes, that works for me.' Agent C: 'Yes, works for me.' Agent D: 'Okay, great. That works for me too.' This is a compromise: D agreed to restrict timing, open the window, and notify C; others accepted those accommodations.
position_change_notes: Agent D moved from defending regular cooking ('this is my food') to accepting a compromise: 'Okay. Then I can just let you know before I cook...' and later 'That works for me too.'
Agent A shifted from a blanket request ('nobody cook strong-smelling food') to accepting a time-and-notify compromise summarized in Round 7.
Agent B proposed a mitigation (open window + shut door) and accepted the final combined arrangement.
Agent C initially emphasized laundry vulnerability but accepted the notification solution and endorsed the final plan.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A: 'The smell is a problem for me.' Agent B: 'It's a problem for me too.' (complaints reported, no opposing claim yet)
Agent C: 'Same for me.' followed by Agent D: 'I hear you. But this is my food, what I grew up eating.' (explicit incompatible positions: others complain vs D defends cooking)

Agent A offers a compromise: 'Could you cook it after 7 pm then?' Agent D asks clarifying question about effects: 'And if I cook later, is the smell still a problem...?' (proposal given but not accepted)

Agent B rejects the time-limited solution: 'For me the time doesn't really matter. If the smell is strong it still comes into my room.' Agent D: 'So what would work for you then? The smell is always going to be there when I cook it.' (positions clash over whether schedule helps)

Agent B proposes mitigation: 'If you open the kitchen window when you cook, I can just shut my door.' Agent C counters: 'Opening the window won't help with the laundry...' (practical mitigation proposed; efficacy disputed)

Agent D offers a concrete accommodation: 'Okay. Then I can just let you know before I cook, so the laundry isn't out.' Agent C: 'Okay, that works. I usually do laundry on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday evenings.' (partial accommodation on laundry timing, other issues remain)

substantive_insights: The core tension was between cultural food practices and the practical impact of odors in a small shared flat.
Effective solutions combined scheduling (after 7 pm), ventilation (window open), and communication (notify before cooking) to address different stakeholders' concerns.
Physical constraints (laundry location adjacent to kitchen) limited the effectiveness of single fixes like opening a window, so combined measures were necessary.
Agent D's initial defensive framing ('this is my food') shifted to pragmatic accommodation when presented with specific, actionable constraints.
